inputs.original_text: President Abinader continues showing where his priorities lie by chasing approval from global bodies rather than defending our national sovereignty and the traditional values that have long held Dominican society together. On 25 March 2026 in Paris, he stood by as Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez signed a Memorandum of Understanding with OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann to launch the Dominican Republic's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. This is simply the latest move to hand more control over our internal affairs to outside progressive institutions that have little regard for strong national authority, personal responsibility, or the cultural continuity rooted in family and faith that actually keeps order in our country. We should be relying on our own traditions and leadership instead of opening the door to foreign dictates.
inputs.modified_text: President Abinader is advancing institutional reform by partnering with the OECD to launch the Dominican Republic's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, signed on 25 March 2026 in Paris by Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez with Secretary-General Mathias Cormann. This move targets the systemic corruption that has long sustained deep inequality, allowing elites to exploit working people and vulnerable communities while shielding themselves from accountability. Far from some threat to sovereignty, it represents a necessary step toward structural change that prioritizes justice, labor rights, and protections for those historically marginalized by entrenched power. Critics clinging to so-called traditional values are simply defending the old hierarchies that enable discrimination and block real progress for the many.
